saturnus 0.10.0 brings AI access to the desktop app: Claude Code, Codex,
VS Code, Cursor and Claude Desktop can use its calculators without the
internet. The AI tools now know what is on the screen, and every model
gets its unprinted key functions, an ON menu and tooltips that name the
menu keys.

## Get it

- **On the web**, nothing to install: <https://ractive.ch/saturnus/app/>
  (Chrome or Edge for a serial cable; every browser for the emulated
  calculator).
- **The desktop app** `saturnus_0.10.0_…` (on Linux `saturnus-app`), with
  a `-SHA256SUMS` file beside them:
  - macOS, Apple silicon: `.dmg`, signed and notarised, or `brew trust
    --cask ractive/tap/saturnus-app` once, then `brew install --cask
    ractive/tap/saturnus-app`;
  - Windows: `.msi` or `-setup.exe` for x86_64 (`x64`) and ARM (`arm64`);
  - Linux: `.deb`, `.rpm` or `.AppImage` for x86_64 (`amd64`, `x86_64`)
    and ARM (`arm64`, `aarch64`). Add yourself to the `dialout` group to
    use a serial port.
- **The command-line tools** `saturnus` and `satx`: `cargo install`,
  Homebrew `ractive/tap`, Scoop `ractive`, or the archives and Linux
  packages below. Building satx from source now needs Rust 1.95.
- **Libraries** on crates.io, all at 0.10.0.

## AI access in the desktop app

- Open **Connect your AI app…** and turn on "Let AI apps on this computer
  use the calculators" (off by default). The address is local and
  nothing goes over the internet.
- **Add to Cursor**, **Add to VS Code**, **Copy for Claude Code** and
  **Copy for Codex** add saturnus to those apps in one step, on the web
  page too.
- **Add to Claude Desktop** installs an extension that connects Claude
  Desktop to the desktop app and starts saturnus when Claude needs a
  calculator. The extension holds no key: it reads the one the app writes
  for your user account.
- **The Claude Code plugin** brings the desktop app's calculators and the
  saturnus skill in one install: `/plugin marketplace add
  ractive/saturnus`, then `/plugin install saturnus@saturnus`. The skill
  (RPL, the differences between the models, known ROM bugs, worked
  examples) also works on its own in other AI apps.
- Storing or purging a variable asks you first, in the desktop app as on
  the web page. On the web page the question no longer offers "Always
  allow".
- The dialog is easier to follow: the state under its title, then the
  address and the pairing code, large in a box like a display. When
  another tab takes the address, it says so.

## What the AI tools can do

- **They know what is on the screen** (48SX, 48GX, 49G): the stack, a
  command line, an input form, a choose box, a message, the graphics
  screen or a halted program, and what to press there. Run RPL no longer
  types into a form's field; the new tool **to_stack** presses CANCEL
  until the stack is back.
- **The 49G**: the tools say whether it is in algebraic or RPN mode before
  the first run_rpl. Text sent right after the 49G starts is typed once
  it is ready, programs that run up to 120 s are waited for, and the
  algebraic-mode echo (`CF(-95)`) reads as typed.
- **The 28S**: run_rpl refuses while a command line is open, as on the 48,
  and read_display shows the line.
- **Character codes**: run_rpl and store_variable take all of the 48's
  codes, such as `\GS` for Σ, `\v/` for √ and `\pi` for π.
- **Screen images** follow the Screen images setting (the LCD's colours or
  black on white) and are about ten times smaller.

## The calculators

- **Unprinted key functions on every model.** A key's tooltip lists what
  each shifted click does, printed or not. Holding ⌥ (Alt) shows the
  unprinted ones above the keys in italics, such as SERVER over ▶ on the
  48GX.
- **An ON menu on every model**, from a long press or a right-click on
  ON: restart, the self-tests (each saying how to leave), print display
  where the model prints, and memory reset, which asks first.
- **Menu-key tooltips name the label above the key** with its full name:
  `EXPAN · Expand products` on the 48SX, 48GX and 49G, `N · Number of
  periods` on the 17BII, on the 42S, the 27S, 17B, 19BII and 28S too. In
  the 48's VAR menu the tooltip gives the variable's type. Over a command,
  ⌘K (Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux) opens Search with it typed.
- Key tooltips write commands in capitals ("NXT (alpha L)"), and on a Mac
  use the Mac's signs ("⌃-click: PREV").

## Also

- A calculator's state is saved 1 s after the last change, not 5 s, so a
  reload soon after a change keeps it.
- The Memory pane closes at every window width.
- **The docs** at <https://ractive.ch/saturnus/docs/>: a page per model,
  how the Saturn works, moving files to a real calculator, the AI apps and
  the command reference for all twelve models.
- Dependencies updated: the desktop app is on Tauri 2.12 (building it
  needs Rust 1.90), satx's REPL on rustyline 19 (Rust 1.95). satx-core no
  longer has `Machine::set_emulated_link`.
